title: Hypotheticals
point: Shift the verb one step into the past to talk about things that aren't true now (if I had…, I'd…) or didn't happen (if I'd known…, I would've…).

sentences.ja: もし車を持ってたら、週末は海までドライブするのになあ。
sentences.text: If I had a car, I'd drive out to the coast on weekends.
sentences.note: Use "I'd" for the result, not "I will": the whole situation is imaginary.

sentences.ja: もっと時間があったら、そのゼミも取りたいんだけど。
sentences.text: If I had more time, I'd take that seminar too.

sentences.ja: 私があなたの立場だったら、教授に直接メールするかな。
sentences.text: If I were you, I'd just email the professor directly.
sentences.note: "If I were you" is the set phrase for advice; "just" makes it sound casual rather than bossy.

sentences.ja: 締め切りが変わったって知ってたら、昨日のうちに出してたよ。
sentences.text: If I'd known the deadline had changed, I would've turned it in yesterday.
sentences.note: In speech "would have" is usually "would've", which sounds like "woulda".

sentences.ja: あの電車に間に合ってたら、面接に遅れなかったのに。
sentences.text: If I'd caught that train, I wouldn't have been late for the interview.

sentences.ja: もっとちゃんと英語を勉強しておけばよかった。
sentences.text: I wish I'd studied English more seriously when I was younger.
sentences.note: Japanese "〜しておけばよかった" is "I wish I'd…" or "I should've…", not "It was good if…".

sentences.ja: 家がもうちょっと駅に近ければいいのに。
sentences.text: I wish my place were a little closer to the station.
sentences.note: "My place" is the natural casual way to say your home or apartment.

sentences.ja: せめてあと一日あればなあ。
sentences.text: If only we had one more day to finish this.

sentences.ja: 彼が手伝ってくれなかったら、引っ越しは終わらなかったと思う。
sentences.text: If he hadn't helped us, we never would've finished the move.

sentences.ja: 宝くじが当たったら、何に使う？
sentences.text: What would you do if you won the lottery?
